generator: box: Blender 4.2.3 headless + trimesh + gltf-transform 4 / meshoptimizer

hosting.jsdelivr_limits: 20 MB per file (all parts below are under 20 MB); 50 MB limit applies only to directory listings, not file links.

conventions.frame: glTF Y-up, front of tractor = -Z, ground (tyre contact) at y=0 - identical to the live default hauler
conventions.composition: A rig is two GLBs (tractor + trailer) loaded and parented under one group named Hauler_<id>. Each part already contains its own Hauler_<...> root node; adopt its children (the SCSRoot_* nodes) into the rig group. World transforms are baked so root_offset_m is [0,0,0] for every v0.1 rig.

canonical_roots.note: Same names the live app's unit-splitter (Unit_tractor / Unit_trailer, presentation gap) already looks for.

loader_requirements: KHR_mesh_quantization (normals int8; positions are untouched float32)
conventions.compression: meshopt FILTER bitstream only: no reorder, no position quantization, node TRS unchanged. Default-rig parts were checked node-by-node against the 30.4 source: 756/756 nodes, max world-position/bbox difference 0 m.
conventions.v02_note: v0.2 tractors are single GLBs with one root node Tractor_<id> (transform baked into that node) plus an empty hitch_fifth_wheel node. Same frame: metres, Y-up, front -Z, tyres y=0, fifth wheel at z=4.263. Normals quantized only; positions float32.

world_alignment.rule: Every rig is baked so its tractor fifth wheel and trailer kingpin sit at z = 4.263 (the default's coupled hook2). The garage floor, world origin and lot origin do not move when rigs change. The display gap between units is still applied at runtime by the existing presentation shift; it is not baked in.

pairing.rule: Any enabled tractor may be paired with any enabled trailer. All hitch points and kingpins share z=4.263. Fifth-wheel heights differ per tractor, so lift/lower the trailer by (tractor.hitch_point.world_m[1] - trailer.kingpin_world_m[1]) at runtime.

tractors.changes: Converted to GLB (Blender 4.2 headless); rotated 180 deg about Y so front = -Z; uniform scale x0.7107 (standard width 2.59 m); tyres seated on y=0; translated so the estimated fifth wheel sits at z=4.263; normals quantized + EXT_meshopt_compression (FILTER); root node Tractor_oga_peterbilt389_luke1985 carries the transform; added empty node hitch_fifth_wheel.

wheelbase_m.source: measured on the scaled model (steer axle to tandem centre); not a published spec

tractors.scale_basis: scaled to standard width 2.59 m (102 in)

hitch_point.method: estimated: z = drive-tandem centre minus 0.20 m, baked to z=4.263; y = raycast: top of frame/deck at hitch z

tractors.notes: Scaled to standard width 2.59 m (102 in) measured across lower body/tyres; source proportions are wider than a real 389, so overall height came out 3.43 m (stack tops) vs ~4.0 m on a real 389. Published 389 spec checked (131 in / 123 in BBC aluminium hood, peterbilt.com/trucks/models/389) but not used for scaling because back-of-cab could not be located reliably on this mesh. Removed 12x12 m ground plane.
